title: Pedestrian Safety on Footpaths Open to Cyclists
what_it_is: Pedestrian Safety on Footpaths Open to Cyclists

sections.label: Cyclist duty of care enforcement
sections.summary: Cyclists must not endanger others; Police will investigate errant cyclists and LTA is stepping up enforcement and developing a National Cyclist Education Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Indeed, although such cycling is allowed, cyclists must always remember that they have a duty of care not to endanger others through inconsiderate, reckless or irresponsible behaviour.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In this incident, as is the case for other accidents, the Police will investigate and, if the cyclists are found to have been errant, the Police will take appropriate action against them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: At the same time, LTA is stepping up enforcement efforts, it is developing a National Cyclist Education Programme with the Singapore Road Safety Council.

sections.label: Active Mobility Advisory Panel review
sections.summary: The Active Mobility Advisory Panel is reviewing rules and safety guidelines for cyclists and personal mobility device users, with a report expected in the second quarter.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The Active Mobility Advisory Panel led by my colleague, Parliamentary Secretary Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal, is also reviewing the rules and safety guidelines for cyclists and users of personal mobility devices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: The panel is expected to release its report in the second quarter of the year.

sections.label: Difficulties in licensing bicycles
sections.summary: Bicycle movement makes drawing the line difficult, and most countries do not have bicycle licensing.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There will be movement of these bikes and we will have to decide where to draw the line.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These would be some of the practical difficulties involved in licensing bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I am not sure whether in China they still maintain such registers but, in fact, most countries do not have licensing for bicycles.

sections.label: Speed limits for cycling
sections.summary: The question asks whether MOT would introduce speed limits for cycling at parks or park connectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
sentences.text: Would MOT introduce speed limits for cycling at parks or park connectors?
